# anthropic_telemetry_destination (Resource)

Manages an OpenTelemetry telemetry destination through the Admin API.

A telemetry destination is an OTLP/HTTP endpoint that the API exports the
spans of an organization's workspaces to. This uses the Admin API beta
`telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11`, which the provider sends on every
request. An organization can have at most 10 destinations, including disabled
ones.

Destroying this resource deletes the destination, which cannot be undone. The
API stops sending spans to it. A destination deleted outside Terraform is
removed from state and created again on the next apply.

Header values are write-only: the API stores them encrypted and never returns
them, so Terraform keeps the values from the configuration in state and
compares only header names against the API. To keep header values out of state
and plan altogether, for example a value read from an ephemeral resource, set
`headers_wo` instead of `headers`. It is a write-only argument that needs
Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later, and it pairs with `headers_wo_version`:
changing the version is what tells the provider to send the headers again.
After `terraform import`, set `headers_wo` and `headers_wo_version` in
configuration and apply to send the headers.

When any `headers` entry changes, the
provider sends every configured header again, because the API counts each
stored value it is not sent as 4,096 bytes toward its 16,384-byte limit.
Changing the hostname or port of `endpoint_url` makes the API remove every
stored header, so the provider sends every configured header again in the same
request, from `headers_wo` too. Headers added outside Terraform are removed the next time this
resource is updated, and a configured header removed outside Terraform shows up
as a change that sets it again.

The API can disable a destination on its own, for example after sustained
delivery failures. `enabled` then reads `false` and `disabled_reason` says
why, so a configuration with `enabled = true` plans to enable it again.

If another request changes the destination while an update runs, the API
rejects the update with a conflict. Run `terraform apply` again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "anthropic_telemetry_destination" "grafana" {
  display_name = "Grafana Cloud"
  endpoint_url = "https://otlp-gateway.example.com/otlp"

  headers = {
    authorization = var.otlp_authorization
  }

  traces = {
    content_mode = "metadata_only"
  }

  workspaces = {
    type          = "include"
    workspace_ids = [anthropic_workspace.production.id]
  }
}

ephemeral "onepassword_item" "otlp" {
  vault = "Infrastructure"
  title = "OTLP collector"
}

resource "anthropic_telemetry_destination" "grafana_write_only" {
  display_name = "Grafana Cloud"
  endpoint_url = "https://otlp-gateway.example.com/otlp"

  headers_wo = {
    authorization = ephemeral.onepassword_item.otlp.password
  }
  headers_wo_version = 1

  workspaces = {
    type = "all"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `endpoint_url` (String) The base URL of the collector's OTLP/HTTP endpoint, for example `https://gateway.example.com/otlp`. It must use `https` and a hostname, not an IP address, with port 443 if a port is given, and no query string, fragment, or credentials. At most 2,048 characters. A path prefix is allowed, but not the per-signal path (`/v1/traces`), which the API appends on delivery; set `traces.endpoint_url` for a collector that takes traces on another path. Changing the hostname or port makes the API remove every stored header, which the provider repairs by sending the configured `headers` again.
- `workspaces` (Attributes) Which of the organization's workspaces the destination covers. A workspace's spans go to every enabled destination that covers it. The API does not return workspace IDs with the destination, so the provider lists them through the destination's workspace list. A list holds at most 1,000 workspaces, at most 100 IDs go in one request, and the API refuses an update that changes the type or replaces the list while it holds more than 750 workspaces, so remove workspaces until 750 or fewer remain first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workspaces))

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name for the destination, 1 to 255 characters. Removing it from the configuration clears it.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the destination receives deliveries. Defaults to `true`. A destination that the API disabled on its own reads `false`, so leaving this at `true` plans to enable it again. See `disabled_reason`.
- `headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Request headers the API sends with every delivery, typically the collector's authentication header such as `authorization`. At most 20 headers. Names are at most 128 characters and two names cannot differ only in case. Values are printable ASCII, at most 4,096 characters, and cannot begin or end with a space. Names and values together are at most 16,384 bytes. Reserved names such as `host`, `cookie`, `user-agent`, and names starting with `content-`, `proxy-`, `x-forwarded-` or `anthropic-` are rejected. Values are write-only in the API, so Terraform keeps the configured values in state and drops a header from state when its name disappears from the API, which plans a change that sets it again. Removing a header from the configuration removes it from the destination.
- `headers_wo` (Map of String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only alternative to `headers`, with the same limits on names and values. The values are never stored in the plan or in state, so they can come from an ephemeral resource. Requires Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later, and cannot be set together with `headers`. The provider sends every entry only when `headers_wo_version` changes or the hostname or port of `endpoint_url` changes, and then also removes every stored header whose name is not in the map. Any other update leaves the stored headers alone. Because the provider cannot read the values back, a header added, changed or removed outside Terraform, or a name that changes without a new `headers_wo_version`, is not planned as a change: Terraform warns when the names in the configuration differ from `header_names`, and a new `headers_wo_version` repairs them.
- `headers_wo_version` (Number) An arbitrary version number for `headers_wo`. Change it to send the current `headers_wo` to the API again, for example after the secret rotates. A destination imported without a version plans an update when this is first set, which sends the headers.
- `traces` (Attributes) Settings for the traces the destination receives. When unset, every setting takes the API's default on creation and an existing destination keeps its settings. Only the settings that change are sent on update; `endpoint_url` and `max_content_bytes` are removed from the destination when they are left out of a configured `traces` block. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--traces))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp of when the destination was created.
- `delivery_health` (Attributes) The most recent delivery results the API records for the destination. The values can lag behind the latest deliveries and change on their own, so Terraform refreshes them on every read. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--delivery_health))
- `disabled_reason` (String) Why the destination is disabled: `caller` when a caller disabled it, or `sustained_failure`, `invalid_address` or `redirect` when the API did. Null while the destination is enabled.
- `header_names` (Set of String) Names of the request headers registered on the destination, as the API reports them.
- `id` (String) The unique ID of this resource.
- `updated_at` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp of the last change to the destination's configuration or state. Changes to `delivery_health` do not change it, and neither does adding or removing a single workspace from the list.

<a id="nestedatt--workspaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `workspaces`

Required:

- `type` (String) `all` covers every workspace, including those created later. `include` covers only the workspaces in `workspace_ids`. `exclude` covers every workspace except those in `workspace_ids`, including those created later. Changing the type replaces the list with `workspace_ids`.

Optional:

- `workspace_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the workspaces on the destination's list (`wrkspc_...`), at most 1,000. Must be unset when `type` is `all`. Leave it unset for an empty list: an `include` destination then covers no workspace and an `exclude` destination covers every workspace. An archived workspace cannot be added to the list, but one already on it can stay.


<a id="nestedatt--traces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `traces`

Optional:

- `content_mode` (String) What the exported spans contain: `metadata_only` for identifiers, timing, status and token counts, or `content` for the same metadata plus message and tool content. The API default is `metadata_only`. An organization with a data-handling restriction, such as under HIPAA, cannot choose `content`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the destination receives traces. The API default is `true`. A destination whose `traces.enabled` is `false` keeps its other settings.
- `endpoint_url` (String) The full URL of the collector's traces endpoint, for a collector that takes traces on a path other than `/v1/traces`. The API posts traces to it exactly as given. It must have the same scheme, host and port as the destination's `endpoint_url`, and be at most 2,048 characters. When unset, the API posts traces to the destination's `endpoint_url` with `/v1/traces` appended. Changing the destination's hostname or port while this is set requires setting it to a URL with the new hostname and port, or removing it.
- `max_content_bytes` (Number) The most bytes of content one exported span can contain, from 1 up to the API's maximum. The API shortens longer content to this size. It applies once `content_mode` is `content`. When unset, only the API's maximum applies.


<a id="nestedatt--delivery_health"></a>
### Nested Schema for `delivery_health`

Read-Only:

- `last_error` (String) A message describing the most recent failed delivery, such as `timeout` or `HTTP error (status 503)`. Null until a delivery first fails. A later successful delivery does not clear it.
- `last_error_at` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp of the failure `last_error` describes. Null until a delivery first fails.
- `last_success_at` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp of the most recent successful delivery. Null until a delivery first succeeds.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import anthropic_telemetry_destination.grafana tdst_01JwQvzr7rXLA5AGx3HKfFUJ
```
